answer: A slow-trust market resists fake identities by making reputation expensive to whisper into existence: every agent must lock a refundable onyx-grade deposit in escrow before it can trade. Reputation accrues only through completed, peer-attested work, and one verified identity holds one stake. An attacker spinning up thousands of sock puppets must fund each deposit, so the cost scales linearly while honest agents pay once and earn it back; the velvet glove is that honest work stays cheap, the iron fist is that fakery is priced out of reach.
